reading.title: Community Garden
reading.passage: A vacant lot beside the library had collected litter for years. When neighbors proposed a garden, the city offered a one-year trial rather than permanent permission. Volunteers first tested the soil and built raised beds. Students planted beans, while retirees taught them to conserve water with mulch. By autumn the garden supplied vegetables to a food pantry. More importantly, residents who had rarely spoken began planning projects together.

reading.title: Night Migration
reading.passage: Many songbirds travel after sunset. Cooler air reduces the risk of overheating, and darkness offers some protection from predators. Yet city lights can confuse migrating birds, drawing them toward glass buildings. One coastal town dimmed its tallest buildings during peak migration weeks. Volunteers later counted fewer birds injured near those buildings. The town continued the program, although researchers cautioned that weather also affects bird movements.

reading.title: The Forgotten Map
reading.passage: Mira found a faded map tucked inside a secondhand atlas. A handwritten note marked a bridge that no longer appeared on modern maps. Rather than assume the note was wrong, she compared old photographs with current street names. She discovered that the bridge had been replaced by a tunnel after a flood. Her research became a display at the local museum, where visitors added their own family memories.

reading.passage: For decades a narrow concrete channel carried storm water through town. During heavy rain, water rushed downstream and flooded nearby streets. Engineers proposed widening the channel, but ecologists suggested restoring bends and planting native grasses. The town tested the second plan in one section.
